conventions.entry: a number 0 to 63 in data/nes_palette.json; 9 entries are not usable
conventions.row: the luma row, index // 16: 0 dark, 1 medium, 2 light, 3 pale
conventions.hue: index % 16: 0 grey, 1 azure, 2 blue, 3 violet, 4 magenta, 5 rose, 6 red, 7 orange, 8 yellow, 9 chartreuse, 10 green, 11 spring, 12 cyan
conventions.lum: relative luminance of the published hex, WCAG coefficients, sRGB transfer curve
conventions.hue_distance: shortest distance on the 13 hue positions 0 to 12
conventions.confidence: stated (the source says it), derived (arithmetic on stated numbers), inference (our reading, not yet verified)

recipes.name: Sixty four outputs, four luma rows of sixteen hues
recipes.use_when: every time a colour is picked by hand, write its entry number and its row, never its hex

recipes.name: The nine dead entries
recipes.use_when: when a checker reports an off-palette colour it is usually one of these nine

recipes.name: Twenty five colours is the whole frame
recipes.use_when: budget a scene before drawing it; sum the two layers and the backdrop

recipes.name: Sharing one colour across the two layers costs two entries
recipes.use_when: when a hero must wear the exact wall colour, count it twice

recipes.name: One backdrop, mirrored at $3F00 and $3F10
recipes.use_when: any scene that wants two different backdrop colours needs two frames

recipes.name: The attribute grid is sixteen by sixteen
recipes.use_when: place a colour change only on a 16 pixel boundary; a 32x32 metatile is the safe unit

recipes.name: Black backdrop is the default and our twelve scene files all use it
recipes.use_when: night, interiors, battles, and any screen whose art already has a dark own shadow

recipes.name: Sky colour as backdrop when the sky is flat
recipes.use_when: day and dusk exteriors where the sky fills the top third and nothing is drawn on it

recipes.name: Spend the backdrop on the field that covers the most 16x16 areas
recipes.use_when: count the areas first: whichever colour owns the most cells becomes the backdrop

recipes.name: A backdrop the sprites also use is a hole
recipes.use_when: when a sprite body sits on the backdrop with no outline, the silhouette disappears

recipes.name: Two backdrops in one level means a transition, not a repaint
recipes.use_when: a level that changes from night to dawn changes the backdrop at a scene cut

recipes.name: A ladder of three: dark, mid, light with one row between rungs
recipes.use_when: the first thing to try for any new surface; a one row gap survives composite blur

recipes.name: The middle entry does the work
recipes.use_when: spend the three entries as outline, body, highlight; leave the outline to the darkest

recipes.name: Dither inside one palette, never across two
recipes.use_when: a 2x2 checker between two entries of the same palette is legal; across palettes it is not

numbers.purposes: second hue, or half a row

recipes.name: One palette per sixteen by sixteen, seam on the boundary
recipes.use_when: build metatiles 16x16 or 32x32 so a wall never mixes two palettes in one area

recipes.name: Sky band: one palette for the whole top rows
recipes.use_when: a gradient in the sky costs one palette if it is dithered, three if it is banded

recipes.name: The ground plane is one palette until the material changes
recipes.use_when: a floor that runs the width of the screen costs one palette; a step to another material costs the second

recipes.name: Two luma rows minimum between a sprite body and the ground it stands on
recipes.use_when: the rule Nayil set for this project; check it per walkable area, not per screen

numbers.why_a_row_gap_alone_is_not_enough: two entries two rows apart can still measure 0.0002 apart in relative luminance, so also check the hex

recipes.name: One row plus a hue jump of four or more, with an outline
recipes.use_when: small props and enemies where the three entries cannot reach two rows

recipes.name: Put the hero body on an extreme row
recipes.use_when: a fixed hero palette can only clear a two row gap if its body sits on row 0 or row 3

recipes.name: Outline on row 0 guarantees one row against any pale ground
recipes.use_when: the outline is what keeps a silhouette readable when the body has to be light

recipes.name: The accent may merge, the body may not
recipes.use_when: if one entry of three has to collide with the background, make it the smallest one

recipes.name: White clothing on a light ground is refused
recipes.use_when: the white blob: a row 3 body over a row 2 or row 3 ground

recipes.name: Black outline, entry 15
recipes.use_when: night, interiors, battles: anywhere the ground is not pale

recipes.name: Dark blue outline, entry 2
recipes.use_when: daylight exteriors and sea; it reads as a shadow instead of a drawn line

recipes.name: Dark brown outline, entry 7 or 8
recipes.use_when: warm interiors, wood, the wardroom, lamplight

recipes.name: An outline colour cannot be shared across sprite palettes
recipes.use_when: only entry 0 is shared storage; a common outline costs one entry in every sprite palette

recipes.name: Never outline lighter than the body
recipes.use_when: an outline brighter than the fill turns the silhouette inside out

recipes.name: Hero palette: Percy (blue and gold), fixed for the whole game
recipes.use_when: every scene draws Percy from these three entries; the scene must adapt its ground, not the hero

recipes.name: Hero palette: Hadrian (near black and purple), fixed for the whole game
recipes.use_when: every scene draws Hadrian from these three entries; the scene must adapt its ground, not the hero

recipes.name: Hero palette: Zander (light blue), fixed for the whole game
recipes.use_when: every scene draws Zander from these three entries; the scene must adapt its ground, not the hero

recipes.name: Hero palette: Konrad (grey and amber), fixed for the whole game
recipes.use_when: every scene draws Konrad from these three entries; the scene must adapt its ground, not the hero

recipes.name: The hero owns sprite palette zero in every scene
recipes.use_when: so a scene can never spend slot zero on an NPC; NPCs and enemies take slots one to three

recipes.name: The hero keeps his three entries when the scene changes
recipes.use_when: a palette swap per scene makes the character read as a different character

numbers.allowed_substitution: none without a new palette decision

recipes.name: Blue against orange is the cheapest contrast we own
recipes.use_when: hero against ground, lamp against night, sea against hull

recipes.name: Green against red is the second pair
recipes.use_when: moss on iron, copper on stone, the sea chest in the wardroom

recipes.name: Grey and black are the third member of any palette
recipes.use_when: when a surface needs to sit next to any hue without arguing, spend one entry on grey

recipes.name: Two hue families per palette, maximum
recipes.use_when: three entries: one family for the surface, one for the accent, and the outline

recipes.name: Do not put rose next to red
recipes.use_when: a one or two step hue move reads as a printing error, not as a second material

recipes.name: Distance is carried by rows, material by hue
recipes.use_when: far things lose a row and keep their hue; that is aerial perspective inside four rows

recipes.name: Night is one row down, not a blue wash
recipes.use_when: take the day palette and move each entry one row darker, keeping the hue

recipes.name: Black backdrop plus a navy sky is the Mother and FF night
recipes.use_when: the sky is an entry, the backdrop is black; the sky never becomes the backdrop at night

numbers.note: described from published screenshots and analyses, no image stored

recipes.name: One pale entry is the whole lamp budget
recipes.use_when: a night scene may spend exactly one entry on a light source; use it for the lamp, the window, the eye

recipes.name: Rim light, not fill light
recipes.use_when: a night sprite keeps its body dark and puts the pale entry on one edge only

recipes.name: Fade to black is four swaps, not a dimmer
recipes.use_when: the PPU has no brightness register a game may use freely, so a fade is a palette rewrite

recipes.name: Flash is three entries to white for two frames
recipes.use_when: a hit flash or a lightning strike rewrites the background palettes, it does not add a sprite

recipes.name: Palette cycling is one entry rotating between two neighbours
recipes.use_when: water, lava, neon, the title flash; rotate an entry and the shape animates for free

recipes.name: Swap the backdrop alone for a lightning frame
recipes.use_when: one byte changes and the whole screen changes, which is the cheapest effect on the console

recipes.name: Every object a palette of its own
recipes.use_when: four background palettes is the hardware, not a preference

numbers.verdict: group by material, not by object

recipes.name: Sprite and ground on the same row
recipes.use_when: the failure our checker should catch first

recipes.name: Five or more colours in one sixteen by sixteen
recipes.use_when: a checker that counts past three plus the backdrop has found a real bug

recipes.name: Pastel mush: three entries on row three
recipes.use_when: three pale entries cannot make a shape; nothing is darker than anything

recipes.name: Black as a background entry and as the backdrop
recipes.use_when: the drawn black and the empty black become one shape, and the art loses its holes

recipes.name: Three rows of one hue
recipes.use_when: a palette that only steps in brightness reads as a flat surface with a gradient

recipes.name: Count the distinct colours in the frame
recipes.use_when: a finished screenshot must measure 25 or fewer

recipes.name: Every sixteen by sixteen area carries three plus the backdrop
recipes.use_when: run this before the palette is called final; it is the rule most amateur art breaks

recipes.name: Sprite body against every background it walks on
recipes.use_when: a sprite is checked against each of the four background palettes, not against the screen average

numbers.fail_action: change the ground palette, not the hero

scene_sets.note: the motorway at night from the car: navy sky, black road, warm lamp glint, cold wing mirror; the plate is the black asphalt
a wet street at night: navy sky, dark grey pavement, warm shop light, ironwork; the plate is the dark grey paving
the quay in the morning: pale sky, rust and rope, harbour green, cold water; the plate is the wet dark stone of the quay, which is what clears Percy's row 2 body by two rows
the corridor: steel plate, blue deck shadow, red hatch, pale pipe run; the deck as specced has no entry that clears Hadrian's row 0 body, so this row fails and the fix is in the card's Q: line
the wardroom: lamp amber on wood, brown shadow under the table, cold window, white cloth; the plate is the dark brown floor shadow
the engine room: grey iron, hazard red, brass pipe run, lamp amber; the hottest scene in the game, so the hero keeps his grey body and takes the amber as rim
the bridge: night sea through the glass, pale instrument card, teal depth, brass fitting; the plate is the dark deck
the shared frame of the four battle strips: sea and steel, night blue, rust and rope, enemy red; the plate is the blue deck shadow
